title: Lever C: per-pocket biome variation (vary carrying-capacity K)
notes:
LEVER C VERDICT — VALIDATED by two fresh-context auditors (builder did not self-validate)

MECHANIC: correct + deterministic + byte-identical OFF. [auditor 1, strongest verification]
- config.pocketCapVariance (default 0 = OFF). At v>0, per-pocket K = cap*(1 - v
  + U[0,2v]) drawn from a FORKED rng substream (rng.fork(0xc)) so the archipelago
  LAYOUT (pocket centres, fertility map) is byte-identical across variance; only
  per-pocket K moves. Founders settle differently (they rejection-sample onto
  biomass) — intended ecology, fully deterministic.
- Auditor 1 did NOT trust the hardcoded baseline: it built a worktree at the
  pre-lever commit (1c68455~1) and RECONSTRUCTED the four baseline hashes from
  scratch -> OFF state is genuinely identical to pre-feature code (ch=1
  82e41dbd/1bdaf0bb, ch=2 7098f748/e1df933e). Float32/Float64 trap real
  (~80% of cases would diverge under a Float32 store; Kcell is Float64). fork()
  purity verified empirically. No hot-path RNG. Clamp upper bound exact (K hits
  60=cap*1.5, never exceeds). hashInto never hashes Kcell/maxCapacity/variance.
  148 tests pass; tsc clean. NO determinism/correctness defects found.
- Non-defect design note (auditor 1): founder-placement threshold = 0.3*GLOBAL
  cap, not per-pocket K (world.ts:93). At high variance + low init, lean islands
  may be under-seeded with founders. Determinism-irrelevant + intentional. Sanity
  -check if lever-C ecology ever skews toward rich pockets.

EFFECT: UNINFORMATIVE in isolation — NOT "tested and failed". [auditor 2]
- CORRECTION to an earlier overclaim: "no trait shows consistent sign" was WRONG.
  satiat~K is all-negative across the three v=0.5 seeds (-0.64/-0.32/-0.28). It is
  still dismissible — the v=0 noise abs-mean (0.473) EXCEEDS the v=0.5 abs-mean
  (0.413), so it is a coin-flip artifact, not a K signal — but it must be named,
  not waved away.
- The null carries NO evidence against the hypothesis, because the experiment was
  structurally incapable of returning a positive:
  1. NO K-COUPLING IN THE ECONOMY. The life-history genes (repro/satiat/birthE)
     are pure energy thresholds; they never read local K, fertility, or biomass.
     Mortality is a flat energy clock (basalCost) identical on rich and lean
     islands. capacityAt is read ONLY by the render overlay + the probe. There is
     no density-dependent vs density-independent mortality regime, so the textbook
     r/K divergence has no mechanism to emerge. A null is the a-priori expectation.
  2. UNDERPOWERED + CONFOUNDED METRIC. n~14 pockets -> critical |r| ~0.53 (p<.05,
     df=12); a moderate true effect (r~0.3-0.4) is invisible. The v=0 baseline is
     NOT a clean zero: capacityAt reads the centre cell, whose K has ~4% spread
     from Gaussian-overlap clamping that correlates with geometry/crowding -> size
     ~K is spuriously +0.18..+0.53 at uniform K (the confound tell). Nearest-centre
     binning also mis-assigns migrants, diluting per-pocket contrast.
  3. DRIFT DOMINATES. minPop 40-105/island; mutationSigma step ~5 energy/birth on
     satiat; ~100 generations in 30k ticks -> drift swamps weak selection.

KEY INSIGHT: Lever C is INERT WITHOUT a K-coupling mechanism. Lever D
(density-dependent mortality, life-sim-cu0o) is exactly that missing coupling and
doubles as Lever C's POSITIVE CONTROL. RE-PROBE Lever C (pocketCapVariance>0 +
biome-divergence.ts) AFTER Lever D lands; only then is the divergence question
answerable.

DECISION: ship the mechanic OFF-by-default as a tuning/experimentation knob. Do
NOT claim it as a diversity driver (unproven) and do NOT claim it failed
(untestable in isolation). [[diversity-levers]] ranking stands: two-food-channels
(lever B) is THE structural lever; biome-variation (C) is conditional on D.

Commits: 1c68455 (Kcell refactor) -> 4433811 (variance) -> b5d0b47 (probe+accessors)
-> 2940c75 (directed metric). Build COMPLETE + validated; effect deferred to post-D re-probe.

notes: OWNER REQUIREMENT — genetic-compatibility gate (core of the design): mating requires the two creatures be genetically SIMILAR, not just nearby. A pair can breed only if their genetic distance < a compatibility threshold (config knob; consider an evolvable per-creature 'choosiness'/mating-radius gene). Enforced consequences: (a) predators (diet~1) and prey (diet~0) CANNOT cross-breed; (b) a creature that wanders across the map to a divergent population CANNOT interbreed instantly if it varies too much from the locals. This makes 'species' a REAL emergent unit (reproductive isolation = biological species concept) and enables sympatric/allopatric speciation — watch lineages split. Needs: a genetic-distance metric (weighted distance over scalar genes, maybe + brain weights + hue), the compatibility threshold check at the mate-encounter step, and it composes with the display/preference genes (preference picks among COMPATIBLE mates). Still MEASURE encounter feasibility first (mate-rarity at 8192 = extinction risk); the compatibility gate makes encounters EVEN rarer, so feasibility probing is doubly important.
